one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent immediately adopted a brittle regex-based XSS sanitizer without exploring a parser-based approach, resulting in incomplete JS removal, intermittent formatting destruction, and a false success claim made only against its own test file—never against the actual evaluation suite.
t_err_evidence: Step 1 creates filter.py using a hardcoded list of event handlers and regex substitutions rather than a robust DOM parser (BeautifulSoup/html.parser tree manipulation); the approach has known gaps (non-enumerated on* attributes, iframe/object/embed tags, obfuscated javascript: URLs) and the whitespace-cleanup line `re.sub(r'\s+>', '>', ...)` already violates the formatting-preservation requirement.
t_commit_evidence: Step 11 rewrites filter.py with the same regex strategy plus additional whitespace normalization (`re.sub(r'\s+>', '>', ...)` and `re.sub(r'\s+\s+', ' ', ...)`), permanently collapsing multi-line formatting. After this rewrite the agent iterates only on regex tuning within the same fundamentally flawed paradigm, with no pivot to a parser-based solution.
t_surface_evidence: Step 9 (cat test.html after first filter run) shows `<a xss')\">`—the regex for javascript: URLs failed to consume the closing quote and parenthesis, leaving a malformed tag; this is the first observable failure signal.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified assumption that a fixed-list regex approach is sufficient to sanitize HTML of all JavaScript—without checking the actual test suite, looking at any existing test harness, or evaluating whether the task required handling obfuscated/edge-case XSS vectors. The premise that regexes over a known list of events would pass the evaluation was never validated.
forewarning_evidence: Step 9 output contains `<a xss')\">`—a malformed tag proving regex failed to fully remove the javascript: href. This contradictory evidence appears before t_commit=11 when the agent rewrites the filter.
